observations: Grey chest freezer with a top-opening lid.
Chrome-finished handle with an integrated lock mechanism.
A blue sticker on the top right of the lid mentions a '3 Years Warranty'.
Power indicator light is illuminated at the bottom right corner in photo 0.
Interior light is functional as seen in photo 1.
Frost is visible on the interior walls, suggesting the cooling system is active.
The freezer contains various food items and containers.
No brand name or model number is legible in the provided photos.

claims.evidence: The interior light and frost indicate it is cooling, but mechanical health cannot be confirmed remotely.

claims.claim: I bought a bigger one that's why am selling
claims.evidence: This is a statement of intent/history that cannot be verified from photos.

risks.risk: Unknown capacity and brand significantly affect market value.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturer's specification plate (usually on the back or side).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic/no-name brand of the smallest standard capacity (approx 100L).

risks.risk: Compressor may be noisy or have been poorly repaired.
risks.proof: A video of the freezer running and a photo of the compressor compartment at the back.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as having a noisy compressor or previous repairs.

risks.risk: Thermostat failure (freezing everything or not reaching temperature).
risks.proof: A photo of a thermometer inside showing a sub-zero temperature.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as having a faulty thermostat.

proof_requests: Photo of the manufacturer's specification plate showing the brand, model, and capacity in liters.
Photo of the back of the unit showing the compressor and cooling coils.
Short video of the unit running to hear the compressor sound.
response.reason: The brand and capacity (liters) are not visible. These are the primary drivers of price for chest freezers in this market. A photo of the specification plate is necessary for an accurate valuation.
